text: {"distance_m": 5, "reasoning_short": "A 2 mm spot at 30% contrast behaves as a small target, so the area-times-contrast trade-off (Ricco's law) applies. Assuming a photopic threshold of about 2% contrast at a roughly 5 arcmin critical diameter, 30% contrast allows a spot about 1.3 arcmin wide. 2 mm subtends that angle at about 2 mm / (1.3 × 2.9e-4 rad) ≈ 5 m. The simple 1 arcmin acuity rule would give about 7 m, but that applies to high-contrast detail."}
